newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INTERVIEW - LITHUANIA'S SHEMETA SEES STABLE T-BILL RATES.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LITHUANIA'S SHEMETA SEES STABLE T-BILL RATES.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Thursday that Treasury bill rates had stabilised near inflation and were expected to stay there.
Rates on one-month T-bills last week reached a low of 7.87 percent while annual inflation in April was 7.3 percent.
"We think that (T-bill) rates should remain at the inflation level," Shemeta told Reuters at a Baltic capital markets conference in the Swedish capital.
"We are also happy with the results from our longer term auctions and believe this shows that the market has faith in our exchange rate policies," he said.
Lithuania plans to launch two-year T-bills in the autumn followed by bills with a five-year maturity.
The switch to longer maturities coincides with the transition from a currency board to a more usual system, where the central bank actively manages the exchange rate.
Analysts say the market's response to the longer maturity T-bills will be a key test of its faith in the government's plans gradually to scrap the currency board.
Shemeta also said the government's fiscal and revenue policies were on track and would beat original expectations.
"We believe that things will be bettter than originally planned," he said.
"Our work on tax collection is already showing positive results," he added.
